originality.rationale: The same-object 2016 t-fold-wheel paper proves only the scalar strong metric dimension and exhibits a minimum set; the retained claim instead classifies every strong resolving set and derives the full size enumerator and all basis counts. Broad and alias searches did not locate an equivalent all-set result.
residual_risks: A poorly indexed paper may use another name for multiple-hub wheels or may enumerate strong bases without using polynomial terminology.
The 2016 same-object paper is decisive for known scalar coverage, but the literature search cannot prove global uniqueness of the all-set theorem.

value.rationale: The result is a natural complete classification on a standard family already studied for its scalar strong metric dimension. It upgrades one optimum value to every feasible set, a factored generating function, exact basis multiplicity, and total count. These data distinguish the combinatorial structure hidden by the scalar invariant and can be reused directly in probabilistic or enumerative questions about strong resolvability.
